title: Audit Log
markdown:
The audit log is a persistent, searchable, append-only record of what the system did — distinct from episodic memory (which biases future LLM behavior). Every event flows through `audit/logger.log_event`, a synchronous SQLite writer (WAL + 5s busy_timeout) that appends one row to the `audit_log` table in `episodic_memory.db`.

### Event types
Rows are tagged by `event_type`, including `chat_turn`, `specialist_consult`, `tool_invocation`, `scheduled_action`, `alert`, `integration_inbound` (Slack / Discord / email / Telegram / Google Chat), plus `knowledge_retrieval`, `cache_event` (one row per model call from every call site — Executive turns, specialist consults (chat turns and workflow steps), research specialists, the research routing and watchlist passes, triage, memory extraction — carrying tokens, cache hits, cost, server-side search count and, inside a research run, its `run_id`), `memory_snapshot`, `committee_review`, `peer_memory`, and the external-signal/monitor events.

### Session & turn context
Each row carries `session_id`, `turn_id`, `actor`, `summary`, `details_json`, `full_json`, and `department`. A `turn_id` (`f"t-{uuid12}"`) is set per Executive turn and propagated automatically via ContextVars to retriever / specialist / tool / cache emits, grouping one user-assistant exchange. `summary` is the searchable column (LIKE, ~300 char cap); `details_json` is structured and not searched.

### Views
- `GET /audit` — filterable list with a "Group by session" toggle and session pills.
- `GET /audit/session/{id}` — full ordered timeline plus a server-derived node/edge graph rendered as a three-pane React Flow chart.

### Invariant
Audit writes never break a chat turn: all writes swallow exceptions and log a warning, and instrumentation observes only — it never touches request building or the cached prompt blocks. Audit is append-only: no UPDATE or DELETE paths exist in product code.

### Durable dedup markers
Alongside `audit_log`, `audit_dedup` holds claim markers: `log(dedup_key=...)`
commits the row+marker atomically under `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, so two racing
writers on one key can never both think they won — the loser reads the
winner's fingerprint and refuses. The email poller's processing-scope
bindings (`mail_scope_binding:v{n}`) and every mail dedup family rely on
this discipline. `mail_scope_bound` is deliberately absent from the public
`EVENT_TYPES`, so `POST /audit/log` cannot mint a binding row; a binding is
trusted only when its marker points back at the exact row, its fields are
well-typed, and its token re-derives from them. Factory reset wipes
`audit_dedup` together with `audit_log` — orphan markers would otherwise
read as unattributable evidence.
